text:
kevin_sales: Quick Nightingale POC soak + burst summary. Ran a 30m soak at 250 qps with scheduled 60s microbursts to 600 qps every 5 minutes. Key asks: 1) pricing delta for a small reserved pool for burst stability, 2) why p99 for short-chat jumped above 1s during bursts, 3) security Q follow-up (BYOK/KMS).

anya_se: can you paste the load profile and command? did we use KV cache or embedding batching for this run?

kevin_sales: loadcmd (via loadbot):

``` 
loadbot exec --target https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  --duration 1800 --concurrency 250 \ 
  --schedule "soak:250:1800,burst:600:60@300s" \ 
  --mix "chat_short:0.7,embed_1024:0.2,long_form:0.1" \ 
  --model redwood/llama-13b:v1-ptq --region us-west-1
```

KV cache: OFF for this run (they wanted cold-cache realism). Embedding batching: enabled with 30ms window.

loadbot: run_complete id=nightingale-2026-05-04 summary: qps=250 sustained, avg_latency=165ms, p95=315ms, p99=1230ms, max=4820ms, errors=0.95% (long-form timeouts + a few 504s during bursts). Artifacts: https://internal.runs/nightingale-2026-05-04.json

fred_infra: infra notes: autoscaler observed burst and requested additional nodes at t+22s; however node attach latency was high (~160s) because the region's dedicated pool returned cold slots. The combination of cold cache (KV off) and long-form requests caused the p99 jump. Also saw occasional proxy CPU saturation for embedding paths when concurrent embedding workers spiked.

anya_se: mitigation suggestions for next run: 1) enable KV cache for short-chat to cut repeated prefix cost, 2) increase burst_window_secs to 240s so autoscale has time to fully attach, 3) set prewarm_nodes=1 for scheduled bursts, 4) raise request_timeout for long_form to 18s to avoid client-side timeouts inflating error rate. Config snippet: 

```json
{
  "kv_cache": true,
  "adaptive_batching": true,
  "embedding_batch_ms": 30,
  "burst_window_secs": 240,
  "prewarm_nodes": 1,
  "request_timeout_secs": 18
}
```

zoe_prod: product constraints from Nightingale: they want p95 < 350ms for mixed workload and p99 < 800ms for short-chat specifically. They also require BYOK with HSM-backed CMK and an encrypted KMS handshake diagram. I'll own the security deliverable.

kevin_sales: pricing ask: can infra give a quick ballpark for a tiny reserved pool (2 x vGPU) used to absorb long-form load during bursts? We need a delta to show tradeoffs.

fred_infra: back-of-envelope: 2 vGPU reserved pool in us-west-1 ~ $3,400/month commit. Expected per-token reduction for long-form when on reserved nodes ~25% (fewer quantization fallbacks and stable KV hits). Assuming Nightingale's usage pattern, mixed-month delta vs hosted-only ~ +$2,200/month but should reduce tail latency and error rate significantly. I'll flag for formal quote from finance.

anya_se: also note operational option: we can do scheduled prewarm API calls before each planned burst window (they do repeat bursts every 5 minutes) to reduce attach to <30s. That combined with KV cache should bring observed p99 for short-chat under 800ms in our lab runs. We should run a verification with KV on and prewarm enabled.

loadbot: marker: run_id=nightingale-2026-05-04 results_uploaded link=https://internal.storage/nightingale-2026-05-04.json

kevin_sales: action items: 
- anya_se: PR runbook with KV-on + prewarm checklist and the snippet above.
- fred_infra: pull autoscale event timings and region allocation logs, and confirm formal reserved quote.
- zoe_prod: deliver KMS flow diagram + completed security questionnaire.
- sales: prepare a 1-page delta (hosted vs 2-node reserved) for the Monday exec call.

anya_se: will run a short verification tomorrow morning with KV enabled and prewarm_nodes=1, embedding_batch_ms=30. I'll post the run summary here.

kevin_sales: thanks all - trying to get Nightingale a clean set of numbers for Monday. :thumbsup:
